title: Authentication
description: Flaws in verifying user identities, managing credentials, enforcing multi-factor challenges, issuing tokens, and validating federation protocols.

attacks.name: Username enumeration
attacks.desc: Deducing valid usernames or email addresses by observing subtle differences in server response codes, error messages ('User not found' vs 'Invalid password'), or response latency.
attacks.prevention: Return uniform login and recovery responses, avoid distinguishable account states, and monitor enumeration attempts.

attacks.name: Password brute force
attacks.desc: Systematically submitting permutations of common passwords against target login portals without adequate rate-limiting or automated throttling in place.
attacks.prevention: Rate-limit login attempts per account and source, add progressive friction, and require MFA for sensitive accounts.

attacks.name: Credential stuffing
attacks.desc: Testing massive databases of breached username/password pairs harvested from third-party compromises against targeted portals to exploit pervasive password reuse.
attacks.prevention: Detect unusual login patterns, block known compromised passwords, and encourage MFA rather than relying only on IP limits.

attacks.name: Password spraying
attacks.desc: Submitting a single highly common password (e.g. SeasonYear!) across thousands of distinct enterprise user accounts at slow intervals to circumvent account lockout thresholds.
attacks.prevention: Apply account-aware rate limits and anomaly detection to low-volume attempts across many usernames.

attacks.name: Default credential login
attacks.desc: Authenticating successfully using well-known vendor standard credentials (admin:admin, guest:guest) that were never rotated during deployment.
attacks.prevention: Change default passwords before service exposure and disable accounts that cannot be secured.

attacks.name: Weak password policy abuse
attacks.desc: Exploiting lax password complexity and length requirements to establish trivially guessable credentials susceptible to fast offline or online dictionary attacks.
attacks.prevention: Screen passwords against breached lists, allow long passphrases, and store only strong salted password hashes.

attacks.name: MFA / 2FA bypass
attacks.desc: Subverting two-factor authentication prompts through direct API endpoint invocation, session state manipulation, forcing legacy protocol fallbacks, or replaying authentication tokens.
attacks.prevention: Bind MFA completion to the same server-side login transaction; never trust client flags that claim a challenge passed.

attacks.name: OTP brute force (short codes)
attacks.desc: Brute-forcing 4-digit or 6-digit one-time passcodes when the verification handler lacks strict attempt limits, rate-limiting, and account-locking mechanisms.
attacks.prevention: Limit OTP attempts per account and challenge, expire codes quickly, and lock or slow repeated failures.

attacks.name: OTP reuse / no expiry
attacks.desc: Reusing previously consumed one-time passcodes or submitting codes long after generation due to missing invalidation flags or absent expiration timestamps.
attacks.prevention: Make each OTP single-use with a short expiry and invalidate earlier codes when issuing a replacement.

attacks.name: OTP bypass via response manipulation
attacks.desc: Intercepting the server's verification response through an intercepting proxy and altering error indicators (such as changing JSON 'status': 400 to 200 or 'success': false to true) to force client-side authentication progression.
attacks.prevention: Verify the challenge result on the server before creating a session; ignore modified client responses.

attacks.name: Remember-me token flaws
attacks.desc: Reverse-engineering persistent 'remember-me' cookies that rely on weak hashes, static usernames, base64-encoded timestamps, or unkeyed user identifiers.
attacks.prevention: Issue high-entropy remember-me tokens, store only hashed tokens server-side, rotate on use, and revoke on logout.

attacks.name: Password reset poisoning
attacks.desc: Manipulating the HTTP Host header during password reset requests, causing generated password recovery links emailed to victims to point directly to an attacker-controlled domain.
attacks.prevention: Generate reset links from a configured trusted origin instead of request Host headers, and validate forwarded hosts.

attacks.name: Reset token predictability
attacks.desc: Generating password recovery tokens derived from predictable seeds (such as millisecond timestamps or sequential IDs), allowing adversaries to precalculate valid reset links.
attacks.prevention: Use cryptographically random reset tokens with sufficient entropy, short expiry, and server-side single-use tracking.

attacks.name: Reset token leakage via Referer
attacks.desc: Leaking secret reset tokens to external services or CDN hosts via the HTTP Referer header when the password reset landing page embeds external images, fonts, or tracking scripts.
attacks.prevention: Keep reset tokens out of URLs sent to third parties; use Referrer-Policy and avoid third-party content on reset pages.

attacks.name: Reset token reuse / no invalidation
attacks.desc: Failing to revoke password reset tokens upon their initial usage or following a successful password change, allowing re-exploitation if intercepted.
attacks.prevention: Invalidate reset tokens after use and when a new token is issued; expire outstanding tokens after password changes.

attacks.name: Security question weakness
attacks.desc: Relying on easily discoverable personal information (mother's maiden name, high school, pet name) for identity recovery that can be harvested from social media.

attacks.name: Account lockout bypass
attacks.desc: Bypassing brute-force account lockout counters by modifying username casing, appending null bytes, inserting whitespaces, or supplying Unicode homoglyphs that the authentication engine normalizes.

attacks.name: CAPTCHA bypass / reuse
attacks.desc: Replaying solved CAPTCHA response tokens, omitting the verification parameter entirely, or defeating automated puzzles using automated solvers or OCR.

attacks.name: Session fixation
attacks.desc: Forcing a victim to adopt an attacker-known session identifier prior to authentication, which the server subsequently elevates to an authenticated state upon login without regenerating the token.

attacks.name: Auth bypass via forced browsing
attacks.desc: Directly navigating to privileged application pages and administrative controllers that fail to verify session status before rendering content or executing actions.

attacks.name: JWT alg: none
attacks.desc: Altering the JSON Web Token header algorithm field to 'none' and stripping the signature block, tricking vulnerable verification libraries into accepting unsigned arbitrary claims.

attacks.name: JWT weak HMAC secret
attacks.desc: Cracking symmetrically signed HS256 JWT tokens offline using dictionary and rule-based wordlists to recover the shared secret and forge arbitrary user claims.

attacks.name: JWT algorithm confusion
attacks.desc: Converting an asymmetric RS256 token verification check to symmetric HS256 by signing the token with the publicly available RSA public key treated as an HMAC secret.

attacks.name: JWT kid injection
attacks.desc: Injecting path traversal sequences (e.g. ../../../dev/null) or SQL payloads into the 'kid' (Key ID) header parameter to force verification against a static or predictable cryptographic key.

attacks.name: JWT jku / x5u header injection
attacks.desc: Supplying an attacker-hosted JWK Set URL within the 'jku' or 'x5u' header parameter to coerce the server into validating the token against an untrusted public key.

attacks.name: JWT expiry not validated
attacks.desc: Accepting expired JWT tokens due to missing validation of the 'exp' claim in the server-side verification middleware.

attacks.name: JWT sub tampering
attacks.desc: Modifying the 'sub' (subject) or role claims inside tokens when backend services fail to verify token integrity signatures or rely on client-decoded tokens.

attacks.name: OAuth open redirect_uri
attacks.desc: Exploiting unvalidated or wildcard redirect_uri parameters in OAuth authorization requests to redirect authorization codes or access tokens to an attacker-controlled server.

attacks.name: OAuth missing state / CSRF
attacks.desc: Failing to generate and validate unguessable 'state' parameters during OAuth handshakes, allowing an attacker to bind their own OAuth identity to an unsuspecting victim's application session.

attacks.name: OAuth implicit flow leakage
attacks.desc: Employing the deprecated OAuth 2.0 Implicit Grant flow where access tokens are returned in URI fragments, exposing tokens to browser histories, script theft, and Referer headers.

attacks.name: OAuth scope escalation
attacks.desc: Modifying authorization request scope parameters to request elevated permissions without receiving explicit re-authorization or consent from the resource owner.

attacks.name: SAML XML signature wrapping
attacks.desc: Altering the XML structure of a SAML response by duplicating or repositioning signed assertions while injecting malicious forged assertions evaluated by the business logic.

attacks.name: SAML assertion forgery
attacks.desc: Generating forged SAML assertions containing arbitrary user identities and administrative entitlements when the Service Provider omits cryptographic signature verification.

attacks.name: SSO misconfiguration
attacks.desc: Flaws in single sign-on metadata exchange, insecure SAML entity IDs, or trusting unverified identity provider claims across enterprise integrations.

attacks.name: LDAP auth injection
attacks.desc: Injecting LDAP filter metacharacters into login forms (e.g. * or )(|(password=*)) ) to manipulate directory search criteria and achieve authentication bypass without valid credentials.

attacks.name: Login timing attack
attacks.desc: Measuring microsecond differences in server processing time during password hashing to distinguish between existing and non-existing accounts.

attacks.name: Auth race condition (TOCTOU)
attacks.desc: Submitting concurrent authentication or registration requests to exploit Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use windows, leading to unauthorized state transitions.

attacks.name: Magic link / passwordless flaws
attacks.desc: Exploiting short lifetimes, unencrypted delivery, predictable token generation, or missing single-use flags in passwordless email or SMS magic login links.

attacks.name: Auth bypass via alternate paths
attacks.desc: Circumventing URL-based access filters and reverse proxy ACLs by altering path casing, doubling slashes, or appending dot segments (e.g. /ADMIN, //admin, /.;/admin).

attacks.name: Login CSRF
attacks.desc: Tricking a user's browser into submitting attacker credentials to a target site, causing the victim's subsequent actions and private data to be captured under the attacker's account.

attacks.name: Password change without current password
attacks.desc: Permitting users to set a new password without validating their existing password, allowing an attacker with temporary session access to lock out the legitimate account owner permanently.

attacks.name: Phone/SMS verification bypass
attacks.desc: Circumventing phone number confirmation steps by tampering with client parameters, spoofing API responses, or omitting validation flags in multi-step verification flows.
